headline: Man City reportedly found guilty on most of 115 charges
paragraphs: Manchester City's Premier League financial-conduct case appears to have gone against the club. Sky Sports and BBC Sport both frame it as based on reports that an independent tribunal found City guilty on the majority of its 115 charges, with the case now moving to appeal; the Guardian's live coverage states the guilty finding more directly, while FourFourTwo cites a report putting the figure at guilty on all but one of the 115. No outlet in today's feed points to an official Premier League statement confirming the result.

Arsenal's Kai Havertz is returning to the club to be assessed after an injury picked up playing for Germany against the Netherlands, per Sky Sports, which also floats Gyokeres and Merino as possible stand-ins. Separately, Sky Sports reports Brentford have opened contract talks with winger Kevin Schade as his form draws interest from Arsenal and Liverpool — a single-outlet rumour with no independent corroboration in today's feed.

Liverpool's stance on Florian Wirtz keeps resurfacing: the BBC's gossip column reported this week that the club will not sanction his departure, and Transfermarkt separately reports Liverpool have knocked back renewed interest — two independent outlets pointing the same way, though neither reports a concrete offer. The Guardian also reports that forward Cody Gakpo has reflected on a difficult summer that ended with his move to Manchester City falling through, closing out that transfer story.
